name: Ridge Flier
body:
Ridge Flier
CR 1

XP 300
N Small animal
Init +0; Senses low-light vision; Perception +6

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 14, flat-footed 13 (+3 Dex, +2 natural, +1 size)
hp 11 (2d8+2)
Fort +4, Ref +6, Will +3

OFFENSE

Speed 10 ft., fly 80 ft. (average)
Melee bite +4 (1d4+1)
Space 5 ft.; Reach 5 ft.

STATISTICS

STR 12, Dex 17, Con 12, Int 1, Wis 14, Cha 10
Base Attack +1; CMB +1, CMD 14
Feats Weapon Finesse
Skills Fly +7, Perception +6; Racial Modifiers +4 Perception
SQ sense intruder, hyper-aggression

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Sense Intruder (Ex)

Ridge fliers have a preternatural ability to sense when a creature has entered their territory. A ridge flier gains a +20 bonus to Perception checks to notice the presence of a creature nearby. This only allows them to know there is a creature within 100 feet of them, they must make a standard Perception check (without the bonus) to pinpoint the intruder.

Hyper-aggression (Ex)

If a ridge flier spots a creature that they do not recognize as part of their flock or other individual they are trained to accept, there is a 10% chance every minute that they will fly into a rage and attack the invading creature. The ridge flier gains a +2 bonus to Strength and Constitution, a +8 bonus to Perception to find the target of its rage, and a -2 penalty to its AC. The rage lasts until the creature is dead or 1 minute, whichever is shorter. The ridge flier cannot end this rage voluntarily.

If the ridge flier enters a combat not already under the effects of the hyper-aggression, or the original target is killed during the combat, the chance that the ridge flier enters the rage is increased to 50% each round. The combat-induced rage is directed at a random qualifying target in sight.

ECOLOGY

Environment mountains, canyons and hilly regions
Organization solitary or pair or flock (3 – 16)
Treasure none

This bird-like creature has a large beak, a membranous dorsal sail fin and a long reptilian tail. They also sport beautiful opalescent plumage along their bodies.

Ridge fliers are an ancient creature more akin to pterosaurs than to birds. They are incredibly territorial and fiercely defend their territory against any creature that comes too close. Generally seen as a nuisance due to their aggression, they have been hunted to extinction in many parts of the world. Their plumage is beautiful and is highly sought after by clothing designers for its unique dark-opalescent nature.

Trainers of these creatures have found that employing a leather hood that covers the eyes and top of the creature’s head (effectively making them blind and deaf, reduces their ability to sense nearby creatures and thus curbs their aggression making them much more manageable, if less useful.
